chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed together, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Brushing the teeth (using the miswak) is from the Sunnah of the Sent Prophets.
ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of using the miswak in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi explicitly categorizes the use of the miswak not merely as a cultural habit but as a 'Sunnah of the Messengers,' linking it to the universal prophetic tradition (Sunnat al-Mursalin). In Shia jurisprudence, this elevates the act to a highly recommended (Mustahabb) practice for maintaining oral hygiene and spiritual purity before prayer. The narration underscores the continuity of physical cleanliness as an integral component of worship across all divine revelations.
